name: Kuwait
summary_text: Kuwait is dangerous for trans visitors — the least hostile of the Gulf states, but not safe. In 2007, Article 198 of the Penal Code criminalised "imitating the opposite sex in any way" (up to 1 year in jail); within two weeks at least 14 people were arrested at checkpoints, coffee shops, and taxis, three were beaten (one into unconsciousness), and heads were shaved as punishment. HRW's 2012 report "They Hunt Us Down for Fun" documented police violence against trans women under this law. However, in February 2022 the Constitutional Court struck down Article 198 as unconstitutional — the only Gulf state to repeal its cross-dressing statute. The repeal has teeth: a cisgender woman arrested over a short haircut won 4,000 KWD in compensation, with the Court of Cassation ruling police had arrested her "without justification." Being visibly trans is no longer a crime in Kuwait. But the repeal is incomplete in practice: HRW reports transgender people "continue to face threats and harassment," and in December 2022 security forces carried out mass deportations of LGBT people under "security" measures. For a trans traveler: no criminal exposure for gender expression itself, courts now provide recourse, but police harassment and deportation risk remain real.

sources.claim_summary: Brian Whitaker's overview essay (2016) on transgender issues in the Middle East: gender segregation and enforced dress codes make trans people especially vulnerable; notes 'The Danish Girl' was banned by censors in Kuwait among other countries; discusses cross-dressing as a crime across the region.

sources.title: Kuwait: Repressive Dress-Code Law Encourages Police Abuse | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jan 2008): 'Kuwait: Repressive Dress-Code Law Encourages Police Abuse' — Penal Code Article 198 criminalising 'imitating the opposite sex' invites arbitrary arrest and abuse of gender-nonconforming people.

sources.title: Kuwait Court Rules Anti-Transgender Law Unconstitutional | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Feb 2022): 'Kuwait Court Rules Anti-Transgender Law Unconstitutional' — the Constitutional Court strikes down the Article 198 'imitating the opposite sex' ban.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Library of Congress entry covers the same Kuwait Constitutional Court ruling striking down Article 198.

sources.title: USDOS – US Department of State (Author): “2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Kuwait”, Document #2107748 - ecoi.net
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Kuwait - significant issues include laws criminalising consensual same-sex sexual conduct between adults 'which were enforced', torture reports, arbitrary detention, restrictions on expression and assembly, and extensive gender-based violence.

sources.title: World Report 2024: Kuwait | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2024 Kuwait chapter: authorities used penal code, national security and cybercrime laws to restrict speech; includes a Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity section; notes gender-segregation decisions at Kuwait University.

sources.title: Steps Forward After the Abolition of Article 198 in Kuwait | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 (July 2024): analysis of steps forward after the abolition of Article 198 - the 2007 amendment criminalising 'imitating the opposite sex in any way' (proposed by Islamist MP Al-Tabtabaei) was struck down by the Constitutional Court in 2022; the article traces the law's origins and impact on gender-nonconforming people.

sources.title: Transgender Discrimination Continues in Kuwait, Despite a Court Ruling - DAWN
sources.claim_summary: DAWN MENA: transgender discrimination continues in Kuwait despite the court ruling - enforcement and social discrimination persist after Article 198 was struck down.

sources.title: Audacity in Adversity: LGBT Activism in the Middle East and North Africa | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (April 2018) 'Audacity in Adversity': LGBT activism in the Middle East and North Africa - includes Kuwait's criminalisation and the annex of laws used to punish same-sex conduct and gender expression across MENA.
